propositions: Grounding finders flag symbols as missing/unverifiable even when a prerequisite ticket (via depends_on) will create them, because the finders only examine origin/main snapshot and ignore the ticket's dependency graph.
The plan-review prose rule states symbols created by prerequisite tickets should be treated as existing, but this rule is not implemented in code.

A two-layer citation system using [rebar:<id>] syntax should verify cross-ticket references deterministically (Layer 1: edge check via depends_on or blocks relations) and then allow LLM coverage judgment (Layer 2: does the cited ticket actually provide the cited functionality).
Layer 1 (det_citation.py) must be advisory-only, never blocking, and must verify citations bidirectionally: P→C via P.depends_on(C) or C.blocks(P), rejecting downstream blocks.

Layer 2 LLM protocol requires the grounding finder to retrieve and affirmatively confirm the cited ticket's file_impact/plan covers the specific missing functionality before crediting the citation; otherwise the missing-symbol finding stands (fail-closed).
Reverse-lookup failures (missing ticket, network error) must be caught and treated as unverified, preventing exceptions from escaping the advisory lane.
